P1.evidence: No setter and no application referenced, so the read-back is N/A. The frame was the standard two-part version: 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at, really build out what it is that you want, and then if everything aligns, we can talk about coaching. If not, that's fine as well.' Agreement was implied by the prospect's earlier 'Let's jump into it' rather than requested. The open question was never asked at all — the rep said 'Alrighty' and the prospect took over with 'So I have a bit of a complicated history, but I'm just going to give you some background.' Everything that followed for four minutes was volunteered, not elicited.

P2.evidence: Age was asked ('you said you were 42?'); height, weight and body fat were volunteered. Training was properly explored — the rep followed up with 'When you do the dumbbell workouts, what does it consist of?' — and diet was asked directly ('What's your food like?'), including a genuinely good commitment question about eating clean six days a week. Sleep and energy were never asked. Occupation was never asked and only emerged incidentally, first as 'I've been a restauranteur my whole life' inside the food answer and then, at the 26-minute mark, as a distribution business, in the context of tax invoicing. The health checks are the serious failure. The prospect volunteered a catastrophic history unprompted and the rep asked exactly one question about it, twelve minutes later, and only about the oldest item: 'I know with the car accident, that sounded like that was a nightmare. Do you have any things that still show up or are completely like, fine?' No question about the four surgeries five months earlier, the three weeks on a ventilator, the hernia repair, the colectomy, or whether any clinician has cleared him for loaded training.

P3.evidence: No goals phase was run — every goal on record was volunteered and the rep's contribution was to confirm them back: 'you want the change, but you also want to push past a plateau. Get leaner. For more muscle as well?' Two exceptional threads were handed over unprompted and both were dropped without a single follow-up. First, identity: 'Growing up, I was always the smallest and skinniest kid in class. So when I see myself in the mirror, it's still, it's that never enough thing.' Second, mortality, from a man who had been on a ventilator five months earlier: 'I'm now at an age where I need to take more care of my health... I would rather be healthy till seventy and not worry about different ailments, especially with my odd background with my health.' Neither was explored. He also has a son in London who is mentioned once, at minute 36, purely as a travel logistics detail. This is the richest goals material in the batch and none of it was worked.

P4.evidence: The gap-naming check ran well, with the rep pre-qualifying him out of the wrong category first: 'some people I've come on here and they're like, I just kind of feel like I need some guides, and it's like, if you need guides, you don't really need coaching. Some people's like, I need someone to wake me up every morning. You don't seem like you're that guy.' The prospect named what he wanted — guidance, feedback, milestones. Everything else was skipped. He has been stuck at 19-20% body fat his entire life and nobody asked what he has tried, what happened, or why it has never shifted, which is the single most obvious root-cause question available.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. None of the four checks was attempted, on a prospect who had spent three weeks on a ventilator five months earlier and who explicitly raised his own mortality horizon. The material for the strongest consequence frame in this corpus was sitting on the table and the rep did not reach for it.

P6.evidence: Only a philosophy alignment check was run — 'Does that align?' — followed by 'Any questions on that whatsoever?'. The prospect then asked for the price himself. Neither the belief question nor the all-in question was asked, so the offer went out against no verbal commitment, and the two things that ultimately deferred the decision, an overlapping app subscription and an accountant conversation, both surfaced only after the number.

P11.evidence: A close was moved toward — the rep laid out next steps and discussed payment methods, currencies and a 50/50 split in detail — so the phase applies. No payment was collected and no link was sent. The Trevor onboarding call was described but not booked. No agreement email, no signature, no welcome email, Skool link or questionnaire. The call ended with the prospect saying he had another call to prep for, after roughly ten minutes of unrelated conversation.

objection_plays.detail: Money surfaced clearly at 00:25:27: 'I personally have no money, but my business is doing very well.' One move ran, and only because the prospect asked for it — 'Is there a way that we can break the payment up into two parts?' produced the 50/50 option. No isolation, no 'HOW place' reframe, no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture questions, despite the prospect having just disclosed zero personal liquidity, an active divorce settlement pressure and a competing subscription. The rep's substitute for the financial picture was the corporate tax route, which is not in the play and which created a compliance exposure rather than qualifying the buyer.

Delay trigger at 00:35:53 — 'give me till the weekend and I'll figure it out'. The rep reframed it as administrative ('it sounds like it's logistics, just figuring out where to pull it from'), which is a reasonable read but is not the play, and then did not convert it into anything: no date, no deposit, no booked call. None of the scripted moves ran.

Timing trigger at 00:36:10 about travel and being in London every three or four months across the six-month term. The play's central argument — things never slow down, and 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled' — is a direct answer. Instead the rep turned it into ten minutes of shared travel conversation and never returned to it, so a live programme-fit question was left open.

Script gap — catastrophic medical history, the most extreme instance in the corpus. Four abdominal surgeries and three weeks on a ventilator ending five months before the call, on top of a colectomy at 23 and a car accident at 18 with brain damage. The playbook has no clearance gate and no stop condition, so nothing in the process interrupted the sale, and a guarantee of a 20 lb load increase on every movement was made to a recently reconstructed abdominal wall. This is not a rep-skill finding, it is a missing control: the script needs a mandatory hold whenever recent surgery is disclosed.

Script gap — invoicing and tax. Nothing in the playbook covers how to answer a business owner asking to route the purchase through a company, and the rep improvised into offering to reword invoices to whatever description the client's accountant wanted. The script needs an explicit prohibition and a scripted answer here, because the improvised one is a legal exposure for the company, not a sales technique.

notes: Forty-six minutes with the richest discovery material in the batch — childhood body image, near-death experience, a lifelong body-fat plateau, a son abroad — and not one of those threads was worked; no goals phase, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and roughly ten minutes of pure travel conversation instead. Two non-negotiable corrections that outrank any selling advice: when a prospect discloses four surgeries and three weeks on a ventilator in the last six months, stop and require clearance before discussing load; and never offer to reword an invoice for a client's tax purposes under any circumstances.
